data.name: Love And Order
data.detailed_description:
In the smallest district of Montreal, the Crown Attorney relies on the legal expertise of its lawyers; backed up by the support of a single hard-working secretary.

This is the story of Dana Larose, a young woman starting her career as a secretary in the Crown Attorney's office. The office is both overworked and understaffed, so you'll have to work out whose projects you help with accordingly.

Will you be able to unravel the mystery being covered up, balance the stress of juggling overtime for everyone, and still manage to find love...?

FEATURES

  • Four dateable characters: Jonathan, Pierre, Ross and Dorothy
  • Deal with many different kinds of work to help everyone out around the office
  • Put in overtime for extra money, but be careful to balance work and pleasure or you'll crack under stress!
  • What secret is being covered up by the Crown Attorney's office? Follow the clues...

reviews.review:
Love And Order is a romance-focused visual novel and dating simulation that tries to give its relationships more structure by surrounding them with the pressures of an ordinary working life. Developed and published by Winter Wolves, it follows Dana Larose as she begins working as a secretary at the Crown Attorney's office in Montreal. Instead of using a school, fantasy kingdom, or glamorous profession as its backdrop, the game builds its story around paperwork, deadlines, coworkers, overtime, and the challenge of maintaining a personal life while holding down a demanding job. It is an unusual setting for the genre, and that difference immediately gives the experience its own identity.

Dana's daily schedule is an important part of the gameplay. The office is understaffed, leaving her with several responsibilities competing for her attention. Players decide how she spends her limited time, which projects she prioritizes, and when additional work is worth the effort. This turns what could have been a conventional visual novel into a lightweight scheduling and resource-management experience. The systems are not complicated enough to rival a dedicated management simulator, but they make choices feel more consequential because progressing in one area can mean sacrificing opportunities elsewhere.

One of the more interesting mechanics involves balancing work and stress. Dana can put in overtime to accomplish additional tasks and earn more money, but excessive work increases the pressure placed on her. Managing this relationship between productivity, finances, free time, and personal well-being becomes part of the player's routine. The mechanic complements the story because Dana is supposed to be a young professional trying to establish herself while still having a life outside the office. Eventually, some of these activities can become repetitive, particularly across multiple playthroughs, but they provide more interaction than simply advancing dialogue.

Romance remains at the heart of the experience. Dana can develop relationships with Jonathan, Pierre, Ross, or Dorothy, giving the player four potential romantic paths. The relatively small selection works in the game's favor because each candidate can remain closely connected to Dana's workplace and personal circumstances. Pursuing a relationship requires spending time appropriately and making decisions that support the desired route, so romance feels connected to the scheduling mechanics instead of existing independently from them. Different relationship possibilities also provide a reason to replay the story after completing one path.

There is more happening inside the Crown Attorney's office than routine administrative work. Dana gradually becomes involved in a mystery concerning secrets hidden within the workplace. This storyline adds intrigue and gives players another motivation to continue beyond career advancement and dating. The investigative aspect should not be mistaken for a full detective or courtroom system, however. Love And Order remains primarily a visual novel and dating simulation, with the mystery functioning as an additional narrative thread rather than a complex evidence-gathering adventure. Even so, it helps give the overall story a stronger sense of direction.

Visually, the game reflects the style and production scale of an older independent visual novel. Anime-inspired character artwork and static backgrounds carry most scenes, while conversations are presented primarily through text. It lacks the elaborate animation and cinematic presentation found in more expensive modern visual novels, but its straightforward approach remains functional. The characters are visually distinctive enough to establish their personalities, while the interface generally keeps attention focused on dialogue, decisions, statistics, and scheduling. Players should expect extensive reading, especially because full voice acting is not a central part of the presentation.

The modest scope becomes both an advantage and a weakness. Love And Order combines romance, office responsibilities, stress, money, scheduling, and mystery, but none of these individual systems becomes particularly sophisticated. Players looking for an elaborate legal drama may be disappointed by the limited emphasis on actual legal proceedings, while management enthusiasts could find the simulation elements too simple. On the other hand, visual novel fans who enjoy having statistics and schedules to manage may appreciate the extra involvement. Its systems provide enough structure to distinguish it from a purely linear story without making the game excessively complicated.

Replay value primarily comes from exploring the different romantic routes and seeing alternative outcomes. Because much of Dana's workplace routine remains familiar between playthroughs, repetition can become noticeable when pursuing every possible relationship. Nevertheless, players who enjoy completing romance routes and achievements have additional incentives to return. The game also includes Steam Cloud support, Steam achievements, trading cards, and partial controller support.

Steam Deck compatibility is not officially rated as Steam Deck Verified or Playable, so it should be treated as having no official Deck compatibility rating. Its lightweight visual-novel design and simple controls may make unofficial play possible through SteamOS and Proton, but this should not be confused with official Valve certification. Since only partial controller support is provided, players may also need to rely on Steam Input, customized controls, or the Deck's trackpads for a more convenient experience.

Love And Order ultimately succeeds more through its unusual combination of ideas than through exceptional depth in any single area. The Crown Attorney's office provides a refreshing setting, Dana is given meaningful responsibilities beyond finding romance, and the mixture of scheduling, stress management, relationships, and mystery keeps the experience from becoming entirely passive. Some dated presentation elements and repetitive management tasks prevent it from reaching the strongest examples of the genre, but it remains an appealing choice for players who like romance visual novels with light simulation mechanics and multiple routes.

Rating: 6/10
